summary: Imaging hangs during post-apply driver stage due to late enumeration of secondary NIC
description:
Issue summary: Several provisioning jobs in our imaging lab are stalling in the 'Post-Apply Drivers' step. The task sequence remains running but does not progress to OOBE
Impact: Blocks workstation provisioning (lab and adhoc service repairs). Lab throughput reduced by ~40% during repro window; escalations to onsite desk technicians. No customer-facing outages.
Observed symptoms: Task sequence timer continues; network stack not fully up for primary OS; device shows second NIC enumerating late (after driver package stage completed). WinPE completes and hands off to OS, but Win32_Process install driver actions hang waiting for device present.
Environment: Imaging lab (us-west), PXE->WinPE 10 22H2, SCCM task sequence v2.3, driver catalog version 2026-03-08. Affected units have an integrated 2.5GbE + embedded modem path (multi-function NIC) or external TB4 dock connected during imaging.
Additional notes: This appears intermittent (20% of units of same model) and correlated with units docked or with certain EC firmware versions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) PXE boot target device to WinPE (image capture/provision flow).
2) Run SCCM task sequence that applies base image and then Post-Apply Drivers step.
3) Ensure device is connected to TB4 dock or has WWAN SIM tray inserted (to reproduce multi-function NIC).

4) Observe Task Sequence logs (SMSTS) and wait for Post-Apply Drivers step to finish — in failing cases this step does not complete and the machine reboots into OOBE with missing drivers or stalls in TS.
logs: SMSTS.log excerpt (winpe): [2026-03-10 09:42:17] ApplyDriverPackages: Waiting for device {PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_15BB} to appear (timeout 120s)
System event: DeviceInstall: Device 'PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_15BB' reported not present during driver install sequence
WinPE shell: driver installer exit code 0 but subsequent plug-and-play event for '2.5GbE' arrives 95s later
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Devon Alvarez: Assigned for initial triage. Collected SMSTS logs from two failing units and one success for comparison.

2026-03-10 13:05 - Maya Chen: Repro in lab: reproduced on Dell 9440 with TB4 dock attached. If dock disconnected before driver stage, task sequence completes. Suspect late PCI enumeration caused by dock/EC ordering.
2026-03-11 09:48 - SRE (Arjun Patel): Looked at firmware inventory; three failing units have EC firmware 1.4.2 while passing units have 1.4.0. Created baseline to test downgrade/upgrade.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Imaging Team (Lina Kostas): Worked a temporary workaround: add a 60s explicit delay before Post-Apply Drivers and retry driver install. That reduced failures in lab from 20% to 5%.
2026-03-13 11:02 - Devon Alvarez: Opened GH PR to add optional delay flag in SCCM task sequence and added logging around PnP events. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/612
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Multi-function NIC (2.5GbE + WWAN) enumerates after driver install step completes, causing driver installer to report device missing and leaving task sequence waiting for device presence.
Hypothesis 2: EC firmware update changed PCI enumeration timing for devices behind TB4/USB-C controller. Correlation seen with EC 1.4.2. Need replicate by flashing EC 1.4.2 to known-good unit.
Triage steps performed: compared SMSTS logs, captured USB/PCI enumeration timelines via WinDbg and PnP tracing, exercised imaging with and without dock attached, tested adding a 60s wait in TS.

Root cause (in progress): Likely timing window between OS boot and PnP event for secondary NIC when either dock present or EC firmware version is newer. Not a Windows bug per se; ordering change at firmware/EC level + driver install assumptions in TS.
resolution: Workaround applied: Imaging Team added conditional 60s pause before Post-Apply Drivers for affected models when dock is connected or when EC firmware >=1.4.2. Documented as temporary workaround in runbook.

Permanent fix plan: 1) Update SCCM task sequence to perform driver apply at a later stage after initial PnP stabilization and add PnP event polling (PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/612). 2) Coordinate with Hardware team to validate EC firmware behavior and push recommended EC firmware (rollback or vendor fix) to repair queue. 3) Re-capture updated golden image with driver staging that tolerates late enumeration.
Follow-ups: Create automated check in imaging validation job to catch late-PnP devices (ticket created to add telemetry). Owner: Devon. Target rollout of TS change: 2026-03-20 after QA.
Status: In Progress — workaround in place in lab; rollout pending QA and vendor coordination.
